1	# Repository Parallelizer
     2	
     3	Manage multiple related git repositories as a single project — with parallel workspaces, branch orchestration, and a web-based GUI.
     4	
     5	## What Is This?
     6	
     7	When a project spans several git repositories, keeping them in sync is tedious: cloning each one, switching branches across all of them, remembering which repos belong together. **Repository Parallelizer** treats a group of repos as one "project" and lets you create isolated **workspaces** — each with its own branch configuration, cloned copies, and a ready-to-open VS Code `.code-workspace` file.
     8	
     9	Set up a project once, then spin up as many parallel workspaces as you need — one for the main branch, one for a feature, one for a hotfix — without stepping on your own toes.
    10	
    11	## Features
    12	
    13	- **Project-based repo grouping** — register repositories once, then combine them into projects.
    14	- **Parallel workspaces** — create multiple independent workspaces per project, each with its own branch assignments and cloned copies.
    15	- **One-click branch switching** — switch branches across all repos in a workspace in a single operation, with conflict detection.
    16	- **VS Code integration** — auto-generated `.code-workspace` files let you open an entire workspace in VS Code instantly.
    17	- **Web GUI** — a built-in browser UI for managing repositories, projects, workspaces, and branches — no terminal required after setup. The project dashboard supports real-time filtering by name/ID/description, repository filtering, and sort by alphabetical or last-activity order.
    18	- **Live git status** — automatic polling shows current branches, uncommitted changes, and unfetched commits at a glance.
    19	- **Workspace health checks** — detect and fix configuration drift (missing repos, stale workspace files).
    20	- **Interactive CLI** — a keyboard-driven terminal menu for quick access to setup, server launch, and documentation generation.
    21	- **Private repo support** — per-host credential management for cloning private repositories.
    22	
    23	## How Does This Compare to Git Worktrees?
    24	
    25	Git worktrees let you check out multiple branches of a **single** repository side by side — great when your entire project lives in one repo. Repository Parallelizer solves a different problem: when your project spans **multiple** repositories that need to move together.
    26	
    27	| | Git Worktrees | Repository Parallelizer |
    28	|---|---|---|
    29	| **Scope** | One repository, multiple branches | Multiple repositories, multiple branches |
    30	| **Branch switching** | Per-repo only | Coordinated across all repos at once |
    31	| **VS Code workspace** | Manual setup | Auto-generated `.code-workspace` files |
    32	| **Status overview** | Per-repo (`git status`) | Aggregated across all repos in a workspace |
    33	
    34	If your project is a single repo, worktrees are the simpler choice. If you're juggling a frontend, backend, shared library, and infrastructure repo that all need to be on the same feature branch — that's where this tool comes in.
    35	
    36	## Requirements
    37	
    38	- **Node.js** >= 18
    39	- **npm** >= 9
    40	- **git** >= 2.28
    41	
    42	## Quick Start
    43	
    44	```bash
    45	# Clone and build
    46	git clone https://github.com/Mistralys/repo-parallelizer.git
    47	cd repo-parallelizer
    48	npm install
    49	npm run build
    50	
    51	# Run the setup wizard to create your config
    52	npm link
    53	paralizer setup
    54	
    55	# Launch the GUI
    56	paralizer serve
    57	```
    58	
    59	The setup wizard walks you through creating a `config.json` with your projects folder and storage location. Once complete, open `http://localhost:4200` in your browser to start managing your repositories.
    60	
    61	### Alternative: run without installing globally
    62	
    63	```bash
    64	# Unix / macOS
    65	./menu.sh
    66	
    67	# Windows
    68	menu.cmd
    69	```
    70	
    71	### CLI commands
    72	
    73	| Command | Description |
    74	|---------|-------------|
    75	| `paralizer` | Open the interactive CLI menu |
    76	| `paralizer serve` | Start the GUI server directly |
    77	| `paralizer setup` | Run the setup wizard |
    78	| `paralizer docs` | Generate project documentation |
    79	
    80	## Start with Windows
    81	
    82	1. Press `Win + R`, type the following command to open your user Startup folder, and press **Enter**:
    83	   ```
    84	   shell:startup
    85	   ```
    86	   *(This opens the folder: `C:\Users\<YourUsername>\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup`)*
    87	
    88	2. In that folder, right-click an empty area and select **New** > **Text Document**.
    89	3. Name it `start-repo-parallelizer.vbs` (ensure you delete the `.txt` extension!).
    90	4. Right-click the new file, select **Edit** (or open it with Notepad/VS Code), and paste the following code into it:
    91	
    92	   ```vbscript
    93	   Set WshShell = CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
    94	   ' 0 means the window will be hidden, so you don't have a lingering terminal
    95	   WshShell.Run "cmd /c paralizer serve", 0
    96	   Set WshShell = Nothing
    97	   ```
    98	
    99	   > **Requires `npm link`** — run `npm link` once in the project folder so `paralizer` is available globally.

1	# Server - Architecture Routes
     2	_SOURCE: REST API route handlers_
     3	# REST API route handlers
     4	```
     5	// Structure of documents
     6	└── src/
     7	    └── server/
     8	        └── routes/
     9	            └── branches.ts
    10	            └── config.ts
    11	            └── error-log.ts
    12	            └── notes.ts
    13	            └── projects.ts
    14	            └── repositories.ts
    15	            └── status.ts
    16	            └── version.ts
    17	            └── workspaces.ts
    18

    20	###  Path: `/src/server/routes/branches.ts`
    21	
    22	```ts
    23	import type { IncomingMessage, ServerResponse } from 'node:http';
    24	import type { Router } from '../router.js';
    25	import type { BranchOrchestrator } from '../../orchestration/branch-orchestrator.js';
    26	import type { WorkspaceManager } from '../../models/workspace/workspace.manager.js';
    27	// NotFoundError is used in the orchestrator catch block (GET branches handler).
    28	import { NotFoundError } from '../../errors.js';
    29	import { parseJsonBody, sendJson, sendError, isPlainObject } from '../requestUtils.js';
    30	import type { BranchInfo } from '../../git/git.types.js';
    31	import type { WorkspaceInfo } from '../../models/workspace/workspace.types.js';
    32	
    33	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    34	// Response shape for the GET branches endpoint
    35	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    36	
    37	export interface BranchesResponse {
    38	    /** Branches grouped by repository ID. */
    39	    branches: Record<string, BranchInfo[]>;
    40	    /** Compiled, sorted, deduplicated branch name suggestions for UI. */
    41	    suggestions: string[];
    42	}
    43	
    44	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    45	// Route registration
    46	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    47	
    48	/**
    49	 * Registers the two branch-related routes nested under a workspace on the
    50	 * provided `Router` instance.
    51	 *
    52	 * | Method | Path                                                      | Success | Failure |
    53	 * |--------|-----------------------------------------------------------|---------|---------|
    54	 * | GET    | /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/branches               | 200     | 404     |
    55	 * | POST   | /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/branches/switch        | 200     | 400/404 |
    56	 *
    57	 * @param router           - The Router to register routes on.
    58	 * @param orchestrator     - Provides `getAvailableBranches()`, `compileBranchSuggestions()`,
    59	 *                           and `switchBranches()`.
    60	 * @param workspaceManager - Used to verify that the requested workspace exists before
    61	 *                           delegating to the orchestrator.
    62	 */
    63	export function registerBranchRoutes(
    64	    router: Router,
    65	    orchestrator: BranchOrchestrator,
    66	    workspaceManager: WorkspaceManager,
    67	): void {
    68	    /**
    69	     * Look up a workspace by project and workspace ID.
    70	     *
    71	     * Sends a `404` response and returns `undefined` when the workspace
    72	     * (or its parent project) cannot be found.
    73	     *
    74	     * @param res         - The outgoing HTTP response (used to send the 404 error).
    75	     * @param projectId   - The ID of the parent project.
    76	     * @param workspaceId - The ID of the workspace to look up.
    77	     * @returns The matching `WorkspaceInfo` on success, or `undefined` when a 404
    78	     *          has already been written to `res`.
    79	     */
    80	    function resolveWorkspace(
    81	        res: ServerResponse,
    82	        projectId: string,
    83	        workspaceId: string,
    84	    ): WorkspaceInfo | undefined {
    85	        try {
    86	            const ws = workspaceManager.getById(projectId, workspaceId);
    87	            if (ws === undefined) {
    88	                sendError(res, 404, `Workspace "${workspaceId}" not found in project "${projectId}".`);
    89	                return undefined;
    90	            }
    91	            return ws;
    92	        } catch (err) {
    93	            sendError(res, 404, err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Not found.');
    94	            return undefined;
    95	        }
    96	    }
    97	
    98	    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    99	    // GET /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/branches
   100	    //   Returns available branches per repository + compiled suggestions.

1	# REST API
     2	
     3	All endpoints are served by the built-in HTTP server on `serverPort` (default `4200`). Request and response bodies are JSON. The GUI SPA is served as static files from the same server.
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## Repositories
     8	
     9	| Method | Path | Success | Error Codes | Description |
    10	|---|---|---|---|---|
    11	| `GET` | `/api/repositories` | 200 | — | List all repositories. |
    12	| `GET` | `/api/repositories/:id` | 200 | 404 | Get a single repository by ID. |
    13	| `POST` | `/api/repositories` | 201 | 400 | Register a new repository. Body: `{ url, name?, id? }`. |
    14	| `PUT` | `/api/repositories/:id` | 200 | 404, 500 | Update repository metadata. Body: `{ name }`. |
    15	| `DELETE` | `/api/repositories/:id` | 204 | 404 | Delete a repository. |
    16	
    17	---
    18	
    19	## Projects
    20	
    21	| Method | Path | Success | Error Codes | Description |
    22	|---|---|---|---|---|
    23	| `GET` | `/api/projects` | 200 | — | List all projects (index entries). |
    24	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:id` | 200 | 404 | Get full project data by ID. Response includes an optional `LastActivity?: string` field (ISO 8601) when the project has recorded git activity via the polling layer; absent on projects that have never been polled. |
    25	| `POST` | `/api/projects` | 201 | 400 | Create a new project. Body: `{ name, repositoryIds, description?, id? }`. |
    26	| `PUT` | `/api/projects/:id` | 200 | 404 | Update project metadata. Body: `{ Name?, Description? }`. |
    27	| `PUT` | `/api/projects/:id/rename` | 200 | 400, 404 | Rename project (change ID). Body: `{ newId }`. |
    28	| `DELETE` | `/api/projects/:id` | 204 | 404 | Delete project and all workspace files. |
    29	| `POST` | `/api/projects/:id/repositories` | 200 | 400, 404 | Add repository to project. Body: `{ repositoryId }`. |
    30	| `DELETE` | `/api/projects/:id/repositories/:repoId` | 204 | 404 | Remove repository from project. |
    31	
    32	---
    33	
    34	## Workspaces
    35	
    36	| Method | Path | Success | Error Codes | Description |
    37	|---|---|---|---|---|
    38	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:id/workspaces` | 200 | 404 | List workspaces in a project. Response includes `Initialized` boolean and `FolderPath` string. |
    39	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid` | 200 | 404 | Get a single workspace. Response includes `Initialized` boolean and `FolderPath` string. |
    40	| `POST` | `/api/projects/:id/workspaces` | 201 | 400, 404 | Create workspace. Body: `{ id, description? }`. |
    41	| `PUT` | `/api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid` | 200 | 400, 404 | Update workspace description and/or notes. Body: `{ description?, notes? }` — at least one field required. 400 if neither field is present or body is not a valid JSON object. Response includes a `Notes` field on the returned `WorkspaceInfo`. |
    42	| `PUT` | `/api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/rename` | 200 | 400, 404 | Rename workspace. Body: `{ newId }`. |
    43	| `DELETE` | `/api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid` | 204 | 404 | Delete workspace (STABLE cannot be deleted). |
    44	| `POST` | `/api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/setup` | 200 | 400, 404, 500 | Initialize workspace on disk (clone repos, generate .code-workspace file). |
    45	| `POST` | `/api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/regenerate-workspace-file` | 200 | 400, 404, 500 | Regenerate the `.code-workspace` file from the current repository list without cloning. Workspace folder must already exist on disk (400 if absent). Body: none. Response: `{ success: true }`. |
    46	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/health` | 200 | 404 | Fetch the health report for a workspace. Returns `{ healthy: boolean, issues: Array<{ type: string, severity: string, message: string, fixAction: string, repositoryId?: string }> }`. Uninitialized workspaces return `{ healthy: true, issues: [] }`. 404 if project or workspace ID is unknown. |
    47	
    48	### `PUT /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid` — Request Body
    49	
    50	At least one field is required. Both fields may be sent together.
    51	
    52	| Field | Type | Required | Description |
    53	|---|---|---|---|
    54	| `description` | `string` | No | Human-readable description for the workspace. |
    55	| `notes` | `string` | No | Free-text notes for the workspace. |
    56	
    57	**400 cases:**
    58	- Body is not a valid JSON object.
    59	- Body contains neither a `description` nor a `notes` field (or both values are non-string types).
    60	
    61	**200 Response:** the full updated `WorkspaceInfo` object, including the `Notes` field (always present as a string; empty string `""` when no notes have been set).
    62	
    63	---
    64	
    65	## Launch
    66	
    67	| Method | Path | Success | Error Codes | Description |
    68	|---|---|---|---|---|
    69	| `POST` | `/api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/launch/vscode` | 200 | 400, 404, 500 | Open the workspace's `.code-workspace` file in VS Code. 404 if the workspace is unknown. 400 with `"Workspace file does not exist. Run setup first."` if the file is missing from disk. 500 + error log entry (Source: `'app-launcher'`, Operation: `'launch-vscode'`) if the OS-level spawn fails. Response: `{ success: true }`. |
    70	| `POST` | `/api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/launch/github-desktop/:rid` | 200 | 400, 404, 500 | Open a repository directory in GitHub Desktop. 404 if the workspace, project, or repository is unknown. 400 with `"Repository directory does not exist. Run setup first."` if the repo directory is missing from disk. 500 + error log entry (Source: `'app-launcher'`, Operation: `'launch-github-desktop'`) if the OS-level spawn fails. Response: `{ success: true }`. |
    71	
    72	---
    73	
    74	## Branches
    75	
    76	| Method | Path | Success | Error Codes | Description |
    77	|---|---|---|---|---|
    78	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/branches` | 200 | 404, 500 | Get all branches per repository + suggestion list. |
    79	| `POST` | `/api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/branches/switch` | 200 | 400, 404, 500 | Switch branches. Body: `{ assignments: { [repoId]: branchName } }`. |
    80	
    81	### `GET .../branches` Response Shape
    82	
    83	```json
    84	{
    85	    "branches": {
    86	        "repo-id": [
    87	            { "name": "main", "isCurrent": true, "isRemote": false, "upstream": "origin/main" }
    88	        ]
    89	    },
    90	    "suggestions": ["main", "develop", "feature/xyz"]
    91	}
    92	```
    93	
    94	### `POST .../branches/switch` Response Shape
    95	
    96	```json
    97	{
    98	    "results": {
    99	        "repo-id": { "success": true, "conflict": false },
   100	        "other-repo": { "success": false, "conflict": true, "error": "merge conflict..." }

   107	## Status
   108	
   109	| Method | Path | Success | Error Codes | Description |
   110	|---|---|---|---|---|
   111	| `GET` | `/api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/status` | 200 | 404 | Get cached git status for all repos in workspace. |
   112	| `POST` | `/api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/status/refresh` | 200 | 404, 500 | Force-refresh git status (fetch + poll). |
   113	
   114	### `GET .../status` Response Shape
   115	
   116	```json
   117	{
   118	    "repo-id": {
   119	        "currentBranch": "main",
   120	        "localCommits": 0,
   121	        "unfetchedCommits": 2,
   122	        "modifiedFiles": 3,
   123	        "lastActivity": "2026-04-08T12:00:00Z",
   124	        "hasConflicts": false
   125	    }
   126	}
   127	```
   128	
   129	---
   130	
   131	## Error Log
   132	
   133	Four endpoints for reading and managing the runtime error log. The log is backed by `{storageFolder}/error-log.json` and capped at `AppConfig.maxErrorLogEntries` entries (default: 500, FIFO eviction).
   134	
   135	| Method | Path | Success | Error Codes | Description |
   136	|---|---|---|---|---|
   137	| `GET` | `/api/error-log` | 200 | — | List error log entries, newest first. Supports filtering and pagination via query params. |
   138	| `GET` | `/api/error-log/sources` | 200 | — | Return sorted distinct `Source` values in the store. |
   139	| `GET` | `/api/error-log/:id` | 200 | 400, 404 | Get a single entry by numeric ID. |
   140	| `DELETE` | `/api/error-log` | 204 | — | Clear all entries. |
   141	
   142	> **Route ordering note:** `/api/error-log/sources` is registered **before** `/api/error-log/:id` so the literal segment `"sources"` is not captured as an `:id` parameter.
   143	
   144	### `GET /api/error-log` — Query Parameters
   145	
   146	| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
   147	|---|---|---|---|
   148	| `severity` | `"error" \| "warning"` | — | Filter by severity. Any other value is silently treated as no filter. |
   149	| `source` | `string` | — | Exact-match filter on the `Source` field. No length cap or allowlist — treat as internal-use only. |
   150	| `limit` | `integer ≥ 0` | `100` | Maximum entries to return. `limit=0` returns an empty `entries` array but `total` is still populated. Negative values are clamped to 0. |
   151	| `offset` | `integer ≥ 0` | `0` | Zero-based offset into the filtered result set. Negative values are treated as 0. |
   152	
   153	> **Note on `limit=0`:** Passing `limit=0` returns `{ entries: [], total: N }`. This is intentional — it is useful for polling the current count without fetching entries. It does **not** mean "return all entries"; omit the parameter entirely to get the default 100.
   154	
   155	### `GET /api/error-log` Response Shape
   156	
   157	```json
   158	{
   159	    "entries": [
   160	        {
   161	            "Id": 42,
   162	            "Timestamp": "2026-04-11T09:00:00.000Z",
   163	            "Severity": "error",
   164	            "Source": "clone",
   165	            "Operation": "cloneRepository",
   166	            "Context": { "RepositoryId": "my-repo" },
   167	            "Message": "git clone failed",
   168	            "Details": "fatal: repository not found"
   169	        }
   170	    ],
   171	    "total": 1
   172	}
   173	```
   174	
   175	`total` is the post-filter, pre-pagination count (i.e. how many entries match the filters before `limit`/`offset` are applied).
   176	
   177	### `GET /api/error-log/:id` — ID Validation
   178	
   179	The `:id` segment must be a **positive integer** (digits only). The following return `400`:
   180	
   181	| Input | Reason |
   182	|---|---|
   183	| `abc` | Non-numeric |
   184	| `12abc` | Mixed alphanumeric |
   185	| `1.5` | Float |
   186	| `0` | ID 0 is invalid; IDs start at 1 |
   187	
   188	### `DELETE /api/error-log` — Security Note
   189	
   190	> ⚠️ **No authentication or authorisation guard.** Any caller that can reach the HTTP server can permanently clear all diagnostic data.
   191	>
   192	> This is acceptable because the server is scoped to `localhost` only. **Do not expose this server beyond localhost without adding an authentication layer** (e.g. a reverse-proxy ACL or an API-key header guard) in front of the DELETE endpoint.
   193	
   194	---
   195	
   196	## Credentials (`/api/config/credentials`)
   197	
   198	Manage named git credential entries stored in the `gitCredentials` array within `config.json`. Each entry has a unique `id`, a human-readable `label`, a `host`, and a `token`. Changes take effect immediately (no server restart required) and are persisted to disk.
   199	
   200	**Token masking:** tokens are never returned in full. The response always shows `****` followed by the last 4 characters (e.g. `****abc1`). Tokens shorter than 4 characters are fully masked as `****`.
   201	
   202	| Method | Path | Success | Error Codes | Description |
   203	|---|---|---|---|---|
   204	| `GET` | `/api/config/credentials` | 200 | — | List all configured credentials with masked tokens. |
   205	| `PUT` | `/api/config/credentials` | 200 | 400 | Add or update a single credential entry. Body: `{ id?, label, host, token }`. |
   206	| `DELETE` | `/api/config/credentials/:id` | 200 | 404 | Remove a single entry by its `id`. |
   207	
   208	### `PUT /api/config/credentials` — Request Body
   209	
   210	| Field | Type | Required | Description |
   211	|---|---|---|---|
   212	| `id` | `string` | No | Unique identifier for the entry. When omitted, an ID is auto-generated from `label` as a kebab-case string (e.g. `"My Token"` → `"my-token"`). When the generated ID is already in use, a numeric suffix is appended (`-2`, `-3`, …). When provided and it matches an existing entry, that entry is updated in-place (upsert). When provided and no existing entry matches, a new entry is created with that ID. |
   213	| `label` | `string` | **Yes** | Human-readable display name (e.g. `"GitHub personal account"`). Must be a non-empty string. |
   214	| `host` | `string` | **Yes** | Hostname this credential applies to (e.g. `"github.com"`). Must be a non-empty string. No format restriction is enforced at this layer. |
   215	| `token` | `string` | **Yes** | Personal Access Token or other credential string. Must be a non-empty string. |
   216	
   217	**400 cases:** missing or invalid `label`, `host`, or `token`; `id` present but empty or not a string.
   218	
   219	### `GET /api/config/credentials` Response
   220	
   221	Returns a `GitCredentialEntry[]` array with tokens masked. An empty array `[]` is returned when no credentials are configured.
   222	
   223	```json
   224	[
   225	    { "id": "github-personal", "label": "GitHub personal account", "host": "github.com", "token": "****abc1" },
   226	    { "id": "gitlab-work",     "label": "GitLab work account",     "host": "gitlab.com", "token": "****xyz9" }
   227	]
   228	```
   229	
   230	### `PUT /api/config/credentials` Request / Response
   231	
   232	**Request body (create — no `id`, auto-generates ID from label):**
   233	```json
   234	{ "label": "GitHub personal account", "host": "github.com", "token": "ghp_fulltoken" }
   235	```
   236	
   237	**Request body (upsert — explicit `id` updates the matching entry in-place):**
   238	```json
   239	{ "id": "github-personal", "label": "GitHub personal account", "host": "github.com", "token": "ghp_newtoken" }
   240	```
   241	
   242	**Response** (full masked array after update):
   243	```json
   244	[
   245	    { "id": "github-personal", "label": "GitHub personal account", "host": "github.com", "token": "****oken" }
   246	]
   247	```
   248	
   249	### `DELETE /api/config/credentials/:id` Response
   250	
   251	**Response** (full masked array after deletion — empty array `[]` when the last entry is removed):
   252	```json
   253	[]
   254	```
   255	
   256	**404** is returned when no entry with the given `id` exists.
   257	
   258	---
   259	
   260	## Polling (`/api/config/polling`)
   261	
   262	Read and update the git polling interval at runtime, without a server restart. Changes take effect immediately (the polling manager is restarted with the new interval) and are persisted to `config.json`.
   263	
   264	| Method | Path | Success | Error Codes | Description |
   265	|---|---|---|---|---|
   266	| `GET` | `/api/config/polling` | 200 | — | Return the current polling interval. |
   267	| `PUT` | `/api/config/polling` | 200 | 400 | Update the polling interval. Body: `{ seconds }`. |
   268	
   269	### Validation (PUT)
   270	
   271	- `seconds`: must be a finite integer **≥ 10**. Fractional values, strings, `null`, `Infinity`, and `NaN` all return `400`.
   272	
   273	### `GET /api/config/polling` Response
   274	
   275	```json
   276	{ "gitPollingIntervalSeconds": 30 }
   277	```
   278	
   279	### `PUT /api/config/polling` Request / Response
   280	
   281	**Request body:**
   282	```json
   283	{ "seconds": 60 }
   284	```
   285	
   286	**Response** (updated value):
   287	```json
   288	{ "gitPollingIntervalSeconds": 60 }
   289	```
   290	
   291	> **Note:** No upper bound is currently enforced. Values up to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` pass validation and would effectively disable polling for the process lifetime. A practical maximum of 86 400 seconds (24 hours) is planned as a follow-up improvement.
   292	
   293	---
   294	
   295	## Webserver URL (`/api/config/webserver-url`)
   296	
   297	Read and update the base URL of the local webserver that serves workspace repositories. When set, the workspace-detail view shows a "Browse" button for each repository row, opening `{webserverUrl}/{projectId}/{workspaceId}/{repoId}/` in a new browser tab. Changes are persisted to `config.json` and take effect immediately.
   298	
   299	| Method | Path | Success | Error Codes | Description |
   300	|---|---|---|---|---|

   346	## Notes Display (`/api/config/notes-display`)
   347	
   348	Read and update the notes view display settings at runtime, without a server restart. Changes take effect immediately (in-memory `appConfig` is mutated) and are persisted to `config.json` via `saveConfigField()`.
   349	
   350	| Method | Path | Success | Error Codes | Description |
   351	|---|---|---|---|---|
   352	| `GET` | `/api/config/notes-display` | 200 | — | Return the current notes display settings. |
   353	| `PUT` | `/api/config/notes-display` | 200 | 400 | Update notes display settings. Body: `{ notesCardHeight?, notesColumns? }` — all fields optional (partial update). |
   354	
   355	### Validation (PUT)
   356	
   357	All fields are optional. Omitting a field leaves the current value unchanged.
   358	
   359	| Field | Type | Range | Description |
   360	|---|---|---|---|
   361	| `notesCardHeight` | integer | `[120, 800]` | Height of each note card in pixels. |
   362	| `notesColumns` | integer | `[1, 6]` | Number of columns in the notes view grid. |
   363	
   364	**400 cases (per field, when provided):**
   365	- Value is not a number → `'Field "notesCardHeight" must be a number.'`
   366	- Value is not a finite integer (e.g. float, `NaN`, `Infinity`) → `'Field "notesCardHeight" must be a finite integer.'`
   367	- Value below minimum → `'Field "notesCardHeight" must be at least 120. Received: N.'`
   368	- Value above maximum → `'Field "notesCardHeight" must be at most 800. Received: N.'`
   369	- Body is not a valid JSON object → `'Request body must be a JSON object.'`
   370	
   371	Same error patterns apply to `notesColumns` (range `[1, 6]`).
   372	
   373	### `GET /api/config/notes-display` Response
   374	
   375	```json

   377	```

   381	**Full update:**
   382	```json
   383	{ "notesCardHeight": 300, "notesColumns": 3 }
   384	```
   385

1	# REST API
     2	
     3	All endpoints are served by the built-in HTTP server on `serverPort` (default `4200`). Request and response bodies are JSON. The GUI SPA is served as static files from the same server.
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## Repositories
     8	
     9	| Method | Path | Success | Error Codes | Description |
    10	|---|---|---|---|---|
    11	| `GET` | `/api/repositories` | 200 | — | List all repositories. |
    12	| `GET` | `/api/repositories/:id` | 200 | 404 | Get a single repository by ID. |
    13	| `POST` | `/api/repositories` | 201 | 400 | Register a new repository. Body: `{ url, name?, id? }`. |
    14	| `PUT` | `/api/repositories/:id` | 200 | 404, 500 | Update repository metadata. Body: `{ name }`. |
    15	| `DELETE` | `/api/repositories/:id` | 204 | 404 | Delete a repository. |
    16	| `PUT` | `/api/repositories/:id/credential` | 200 | 400, 404 | Assign or clear a git credential for a repository. Body: `{ credentialId: string \| null }`. |
    17	| `GET` | `/api/repositories/:id/credential-options` | 200 | 404 | List credentials compatible with the repository's host, with tokens masked. |
    18	
    19	### `PUT /api/repositories/:id/credential` — Assign or Clear a Credential
    20	
    21	Associates a configured git credential with a repository, or clears any existing association.
    22	
    23	**Request body:**
    24	
    25	| Field | Type | Required | Description |
    26	|---|---|---|---|
    27	| `credentialId` | `string \| null` | **Yes** | ID of the credential to assign. Pass `null` to clear the current association. Must reference an entry in `appConfig.gitCredentials` when a string. |
    28	
    29	**400 cases:**
    30	- `credentialId` is not a string and not `null` (e.g. missing field, number, boolean, object).
    31	- `credentialId` is a string that does not match any configured credential ID.
    32	
    33	**404:** repository not found.
    34	
    35	**200 Response:** the full updated `Repository` object.
    36	
    37	> **Null-clear semantics:** when `credentialId` is `null`, the `CredentialId` field is **removed** from the persisted repository record entirely — it is not stored as `null`. A repository with no credential has no `CredentialId` key in its JSON.
    38	
    39	> **Known limitation — host/credential coherence:** the API validates that the referenced credential *exists* in the application config, but does **not** verify that `credential.host` matches the repository URL's hostname before persisting the association. A credential configured for `host-a.example.com` can therefore be assigned to a repository whose URL resolves to `host-b.example.com`. In that case the token for `host-a` will be injected into git operations targeting `host-b`. This is a known design gap documented in `src/git/git-credentials.ts`. Impact is limited to the localhost-only threat model, but callers should ensure the credential's host matches the repository's URL host.
    40	
    41	**Request body (assign):**
    42	```json
    43	{ "credentialId": "github-personal" }
    44	```
    45	
    46	**Request body (clear):**
    47	```json
    48	{ "credentialId": null }
    49	```
    50	
    51	**Response (200):**
    52	```json
    53	{
    54	    "Id": "my-repo",
    55	    "Url": "https://github.com/org/my-repo.git",
    56	    "Name": "my-repo",
    57	    "CredentialId": "github-personal"
    58	}
    59	```
    60	
    61	---
    62	
    63	### `GET /api/repositories/:id/credential-options` — List Compatible Credentials
    64	
    65	Returns the subset of configured git credentials whose `host` matches the repository's remote URL hostname. Tokens are always masked before being sent to the client.
    66	
    67	**404:** repository not found.
    68	
    69	**200 Response shape:**
    70	
    71	```json
    72	{
    73	    "credentials": [
    74	        { "id": "github-personal", "label": "GitHub personal account", "host": "github.com", "token": "***" }
    75	    ],
    76	    "autoSelected": "github-personal"
    77	}
    78	```
    79	
    80	| Field | Type | Description |
    81	|---|---|---|
    82	| `credentials` | `GitCredentialEntry[]` | Credentials whose `host` matches the repository URL's hostname. Tokens are replaced with `"***"`. Empty array `[]` when no credentials match or when the repository uses a non-HTTPS URL (e.g. SSH). |
    83	| `autoSelected` | `string` *(optional)* | ID of the sole matching credential. **Present only when `credentials` contains exactly one entry.** Omitted when zero or two-or-more credentials match. |
    84	
    85	> **SSH / non-HTTPS URLs:** repositories whose URL is not an HTTPS URL (e.g. `git@github.com:org/repo.git`) always return `{ "credentials": [] }` with no `autoSelected`. The host cannot be extracted from SSH URLs, so no credentials are ever shown for them.
